- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peak heights when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecast lows when sentiment is negative or trending down.
- Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes; cap forecast increases following spikes to prevent overshoot.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce it; if below, raise it.
- Adjust horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen sentiment-driven momentum in longer horizons.
- Penalize forecasts that ignore recent sentiment reversal; if sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast peak and shift downward.
- Use sentiment as a multiplier: if sentiment > 0.6, apply 10-15% downward adjustment to forecast; if sentiment < 0.3, apply 10-15% upward adjustment.
